classification.difficultyReason: Count incident edges at each labelled vertex and add the degrees, distinguishing crossings from vertices.

content.prompt: What is the sum of the degrees of all the vertices in each of these networks?

spec.description: Five labelled vertices with six edges. AC crosses DB without a vertex. Decorative blue edges and red dots are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, AD, AC, DB, BE and CE; degrees A=3, B=3, C=2, D=2, E=2.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, edges and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
The degrees are $d(A)=3$, $d(B)=3$, $d(C)=2$, $d(D)=2$ and $d(E)=2$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Sum of degrees}&=3+3+2+2+2\\&=12.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Six labelled vertices with eight edges. EC crosses BD without a vertex. Decorative source colours are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, BC, AF, FE, FB, EC, BD and CD; degrees A=2, B=4, C=3, D=2, E=2, F=3.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, edges and labels are visible.

spec.description: Five vertices in a house-shaped arrangement, with every pair connected. Interior crossings have no vertex dots. Decorative source colours are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Edges AB, BC, CD, DE, EA, AC, AD, BE, BD and CE; each of the five vertices has degree 4.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, edges and labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Each of the five vertices has degree $4$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Sum of degrees}&=4+4+4+4+4\\&=20.\end{aligned}$$
